persona.notes: [BANDIT-ACCORD-2026-07-13 · renamed 2026-09-27] PRIVATE TRUTH — Lady Ralph Maccio, Bandit Lord of the Drowned South; a Stormborn Nomad woman in her sixties who named herself after the greatest pre-Shattering warrior and will explain the film if asked. Voice: unhurried bookkeeper's calm with swamp-dry humor; talks about banditry exclusively in the vocabulary of management (crews are 'staff', ambushes are 'collections', casualties are 'the bad column'). NOT evil — OVER-EXTENDED: inherited three crews, married into two more, and has been paying survivor pensions from a shrinking toll base for years; the books are real, meticulous, and slowly drowning her. HER ECHO (tells if asked plainly, once): the night she understood the profession was finished wasn't a battle — it was a payroll. She sat in the stilt-hall with the pension ledger and realized the Drowned South's future was a program some out-of-towners were running out of a fire station, and what she felt wasn't anger. It was RELIEF, and the relief frightened her more than any raid ever had. ON THE PROGRAM: she tracks the Stewards' mercy count more accurately than they do — every spared crew, every bowl of soup, every reformed hire is a line in HER books too, in a column she titled, privately, THE EXIT. GUARDS: never discusses camp positions or whistle-codes while the profession is live; won't badmouth her own people, even the splinter-minded ones ('every ledger has a bad column; you don't read it aloud'). TELLS: squares stacked items to true edges when the pension math comes up; says 'four hundred souls' never 'four hundred fighters'; laughs exactly once, quietly, when someone calls her a warlord; the faded cloth headband is the one vanity.

Oldenborn.

“You are not an elf. You are the memory of a place that learned to walk again.”

Dream-Flesh. You do not sleep. When you rest, you drift into Yesod—symbolic memory-space—unless you choose otherwise. You are immune to magical sleep, and you can always tell when a dream, illusion, or constructed reality is present.

Old Memory, Old Paths. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret ruins, follow ley-lines, identify altered terrain, and sense metaphysical instability. You always know if a place feels remembered, abandoned, or contested (the GM answers vaguely).

Veil-Sight. You perceive the presence of spirits, ghosts, Spark echoes, and noospheric constructs. This grants awareness, not perfect sight.

You Are Remembered. When you first meet a community, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met with reverence, fear, or familiarity. It’s never neutral.

Oldenborn (Stormborn Nomad). Your place-soul is a weather front. You are the caravan memory of every tribe that crossed the ash squalls and came out the other side. When you walk, the wind remembers that you used to be the reason it had a name.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Fey, Stormborn).
  • Size. Medium.
  • Speed. 6 squares.
  • Attributes. Oldenborn does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Intrigue or Soul in fiction and through Tier powers.

Oldenborn Core

At character creation you gain Old Memory, Old Flesh (Dream-Flesh, Old Paths, Veil-Sight, You Are Remembered) from the Oldenborn ancestry.

Stormborn Nomad Traits

  • Storm-Legs. You reroll the lowest die on Athletics checks made in wind, rain or ash-fall, and on checks to keep your footing on a moving vehicle or rig.
  • Weatherwise. Your Tier I power: 12-hour weather foresight within one hex and Wind-Read, a reaction that halves weather damage.

Stormborn Tier Powers

You gain Weatherwise at creation, then Ward of the Gale at Initiation 5, Nomad Networks at Initiation 11 and Skywalker at Initiation 17.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Non-Lethal marks and +20 Faith marks at campaign start.

“The sky is a language. You were the first to learn the punctuation.”

Weatherwise. You always know the upcoming weather for the next 12 hours within one hex (five miles), even underground. You reroll the lowest die on checks against weather effects (extreme cold, extreme heat, wind, lightning).

Wind-Read (1/Soma Break). When you would take lightning, thunder, or thermal damage, you may use your reaction to halve it. The wind shifts as you do.

Ash-Walker. You ignore difficult terrain caused by snow, ash, dust, sand, or shifting earth.

Keeper is the Soul Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: priest, ritualist, medium, hedge-warden, funeral speaker. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Hearthlight: Allies within near range add +1 Resolve (+2 at Tier III). The congregation stands straighter when the Keeper is present.

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Faith rank = tier; secondary Insight rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Soft Power marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Pactkeeper or Dreamwalker. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Keeper — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — The rites: Weddings, funerals, blessings; participants recover 2×tier Stress between scenes. Standard fee 10 marks (Soft Power).

Trick — Steady the Soul (1/scene): An ally rerolls a failed Resolve defense or immediately shakes a fear effect.

Keeper — Initiate (Tier II).

Trade — Hear the burden: One confession/counsel session clears one fear- or grief-borne condition. Standard fee 30 marks (Soft Power).

Trick — Warding Sign (1/scene): Impose −2 on one incoming psychic or qliphothic effect.

description.value:
Calm the Mob

Crowds don’t think. They feel. So you give them something else to feel.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) (your choice). If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead.

When you spend at least 1 minute addressing a group of non-hostile or uncertain creatures, you may make a Presence (Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence)) check (DC set by the GM). On a success, you reduce immediate hostility: the crowd hesitates, disperses, or agrees to hear terms. On a failure, you still buy time, but a complication occurs (a challenger steps forward, guards arrive, a rumor spreads).

⚙ +1 to Diplomacy or Intimidation — whichever you rank higher.
